scams.name: Pickpocketing in Tourist Areas
scams.description: Pickpockets operate in crowded tourist areas throughout Bordeaux, particularly at Place de la Bourse, along Rue Sainte-Catherine (one of Europe's longest pedestrian shopping streets), and near the Miroir d'Eau. Thieves work in teams, using distraction techniques while accomplices steal wallets, phones, and valuables. They often target tourists who are taking photos or consulting maps.
scams.avoidance: Use anti-theft bags with hidden compartments. Keep wallets in front pockets, never back pockets. Avoid displaying expensive jewelry or electronics. Stay alert in crowded areas. Keep bags zipped and in front of your body.
scams.location: Place de la Bourse, Rue Sainte-Catherine, Miroir d'Eau, tourist landmarks

scams.name: Train Station Theft
scams.description: Bordeaux Saint-Jean train station attracts pickpockets who target confused tourists carrying luggage. A common tactic involves groups of 4-6 people pushing onto trains just before doors close, crowding targets while accomplices steal valuables, then hopping off as doors close. Thieves also operate near ticket machines and in crowded platform areas.
scams.avoidance: Keep bags in front of you and secured at all times. Be extra vigilant when boarding trains. Don't put phones or wallets in easily accessible pockets. Watch for people crowding you unnecessarily. Board trains early rather than rushing at the last moment.
scams.location: Gare de Bordeaux Saint-Jean, train platforms, ticket areas

scams.name: The Petition Clipboard Scam
scams.description: Scammers approach tourists with clipboards asking them to sign a petition, often claiming to support deaf children or a charitable cause. While the tourist is distracted reading and signing, an accomplice steals their wallet, phone, or valuables from bags or pockets. Sometimes the petitioner themselves will demand a donation after signing, becoming aggressive if refused.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline and keep walking. Never stop for clipboard solicitors. Keep hands on your belongings. Say 'non merci' firmly while continuing to move. Never sign anything on the street.
scams.location: Tourist areas, near monuments, pedestrian zones

scams.name: The Friendship Bracelet Trap
scams.description: A stranger approaches and begins tying a colorful string bracelet on your wrist as a supposed 'gift' or sign of friendship. Once the bracelet is tied, they aggressively demand payment, often 10-20 euros. They refuse to take the bracelet back and may create a scene to pressure payment. Meanwhile, accomplices may use the distraction to pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets or crossed. Firmly refuse any 'gifts' from strangers. Say 'non' and walk away quickly. Never let strangers touch your hands or wrists. If a bracelet is tied, refuse to pay and walk toward police.
scams.location: Tourist areas, near cafes and restaurants, pedestrian zones

scams.name: The Gold Ring Trick
scams.description: A scammer pretends to 'find' a gold ring on the ground near you and insists you should have it, claiming it doesn't fit them or suggesting you can sell it. They then ask for a small finder's fee or payment. The ring is worthless brass or fake gold. This scam is particularly common throughout France and targets tourists who appear kind or confused.
scams.avoidance: Ignore anyone who approaches with a 'found' ring. Keep walking without engaging. Say 'Ce n'est pas à moi' (It's not mine) and walk away. Remember that real gold rings are never given away by strangers.
scams.location: Near tourist attractions, parks, riverside walkways

scams.name: Fake Police Wallet Inspection
scams.description: Scammers posing as plainclothes police officers flash fake badges and demand to inspect your wallet for 'counterfeit currency.' They work in pairs: one may pretend to be a drug dealer to engage you, then the fake officer appears to 'investigate.' While examining your cash, they palm bills. Real French police never ask to see your wallet contents on the street.
scams.avoidance: Real police only ask to see ID documents, not wallets. Request to see official identification clearly. Insist on going to the nearest police station. Call 17 (police) if uncertain. Never hand over your wallet to anyone on the street.
scams.location: Tourist areas, metro stations, busy streets

scams.name: Unlicensed Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Unlicensed taxi drivers approach tourists at Bordeaux-Merignac Airport or Gare Saint-Jean, offering rides at inflated prices. They may claim there's a taxi strike or that official taxis are unavailable. These unofficial drivers can charge 2-3 times the normal fare and may not be insured. Some use rigged meters or claim the meter is broken.
scams.avoidance: Only use taxis from official taxi ranks. Look for vehicles with official taxi signage and roof lights. Use ride-sharing apps like Uber or Bolt for transparent pricing. Always confirm the fare before getting in. Note the driver's license number displayed in the vehicle.
scams.location: Bordeaux-Merignac Airport, Gare Saint-Jean train station

scams.name: Restaurant Menu Overcharging
scams.description: Some restaurants in tourist areas show tourists different menus with higher prices, add hidden charges for bread, water, or table settings, or charge for items not ordered. Staff may also substitute cheaper wine when premium glasses are ordered. Bills may include undisclosed service charges or inflated prices for tourists, especially Americans.
scams.avoidance: Check that menus display prices (legally required in France). Compare printed menu prices to your bill. Ask 'une carafe d'eau' for free tap water. Verify wine bottle labels match what you ordered. Avoid restaurants without posted prices.
scams.location: Tourist areas, restaurants near major attractions

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Card Theft
scams.description: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs to capture card details and PINs. These devices blend with the ATM's original hardware and are hard to detect. Scammers also use distraction techniques: one person engages you while another watches you enter your PIN or manipulates the machine to trap your card.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours. Inspect card slots for loose attachments. Cover keypad when entering PIN. Never accept help from strangers at ATMs. If card is trapped, don't leave and call your bank immediately.
scams.location: Tourist areas, train stations, shopping districts

scams.name: Rose Seller Scam
scams.description: Men approach couples or women at restaurant terraces and outdoor cafes, offering a 'free' rose as a romantic gesture. Once the rose is accepted or touched, they aggressively demand payment of 5-10 euros. They refuse to take the rose back and create uncomfortable confrontations. Sometimes accomplices use this distraction to pickpocket victims.
scams.avoidance: Decline firmly and keep your hands away. Avoid touching offered items. Say 'non merci' without stopping. Alert restaurant staff if sellers become aggressive.
scams.location: Restaurant terraces, outdoor cafes, riverside areas, romantic spots

scams.name: Tram and Bus Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets operate on Bordeaux's tram network and buses, particularly during rush hours and on routes serving tourist areas. Thieves create distractions by bumping into victims or 'helping' with bags while accomplices steal valuables. At stops near tourist destinations, thieves may grab phones or bags just as doors are closing.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables in front pockets or secure inside bags. Stay alert especially near doors. Be wary of anyone offering unsolicited help. Avoid standing near doors with easily accessible items.
scams.location: Bordeaux tram lines, buses, stops near tourist attractions

scams.name: Fake Accommodation Listings
scams.description: Scammers create fake Airbnb or rental listings using photos from legitimate properties, offering attractive prices in desirable locations. They request payment via wire transfer or cryptocurrency outside the official platform, then disappear. Tourists arrive to find the property doesn't exist or belongs to someone else. France is a hotspot for this scam.
scams.avoidance: Only book through official platforms and pay through their systems. Be suspicious of unusually low prices. Never wire money directly. Verify listings have reviews and host history. Use Google Street View to verify property exists.
scams.location: Online booking platforms, social media advertisements
